title: fine-grained-causal-profiling-for-multi-kernel-paths-2026
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes a repeatable, low-risk process for performing fine-grained causal profiling across multi-kernel execution paths in the Redwood serving runtime. It targets cases where a single inference request may exercise multiple kernels (attention variants, fused matmuls, quantized vs FP16 paths) and where attribution of end-to-end latency or tail spikes to a specific kernel, combination of kernels, or scheduling interaction is uncertain.

Audience:
- Serving runtime engineers
- Oncall SREs investigating tail latency
- Profiling / performance owners evaluating kernel rollouts

Goals:
1) Produce a causal hypothesis ("kernel X caused tail at 99.9p") with an associated confidence score and required evidence.
2) Generate a minimal, reproducible profiling experiment that isolates the suspected kernel path and quantifies its impact on: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU occupancy, SM stall time, and memory bandwidth.
3) Provide clear remediation guidance (rollforward/rollback, kernel knobs, scheduling policy changes).

When to use:
- New kernel variant rollout shows unexpected tail increase in canary or production shadowing.
- Mixed workload exposes previously unseen interference between kernels (e.g., sparse attention + fused softmax).
- Quantization rollout correlated with higher variance across cohorts.

Prerequisites:
- Access to trace IDs for affected requests and the consolidated trace store (trace-id -> kernel sequence).
- Profiling lab with the same accelerator family and driver stack as production.
- Baseline microbenchmarks for each kernel variant (available in /benchmarks/kernel-microbenchmarks).
- SLO targets and alert thresholds (example: p99 <= 1200ms for chat.route-alpha).

Procedure (step-by-step):
1) Triage and hypothesis formation
   a. Collect representative request traces for the incident window (use trace exporter: rwd-trace-export --start <ts> --end <ts> --label incident-42).
   b. Build a candidate list of kernels observed in the slow traces, ordered by aggregated kernel time.
   c. For each candidate kernel, capture: kernel name, variant tag, callsite (model shard id), observed kernel time distribution, and upstream queue wait time.

2) Causal probing via selective shadowing
   a. Create a shadow cohort in the profiling lab that replays the same trace corpus but forces a single kernel variant at a time (kernel override injection).
   b. Run 500–2000 replayed requests across varying concurrency shapes (1, 4, 16) and collect full-device perf counters (SM utilization, L2 read/write, DRAM BW).
   c. Compare distributions and compute delta metrics: delta_p99_ms, delta_occ_pct, delta_L2_miss_rate.

3) Interference experiments (pairwise)
   a. If multiple kernels are plausible, run pairwise interleaving experiments (A-only, B-only, A+B co-scheduled) to detect emergent interactions.
   b. Capture cross-correlation of latency with GPU scheduler backpressure signals and kernel start time jitter.

4) Controlled perturbations and causal inference scoring
   a. Apply small, safe perturbations: tensor packing/unpacking flags, reducing the kernel launch grid size by 10%, or enabling a single safety-fallback path.
   b. Use the following scoring rubric to assign confidence: EvidenceScore = 0.5*(delta_p99_normalized) + 0.3*(occupancy_change_normalized) + 0.2*(repro_rate). Normalization bounds are defined in the Appendix.

5) Remediation play
   a. If EvidenceScore >= 0.7: prepare an emergency canary rollback for the kernel variant with a one-hour monitor window.
   b. If 0.4 <= EvidenceScore < 0.7: open a kernel regression ticket, schedule a non-disruptive A/B test with shadow routing for 48 hours.
   c. If EvidenceScore < 0.4: capture experiment artifacts, label the hypothesis as low confidence, and schedule deeper instrumentation (see Appendix).

Observability checklist (data to collect):
- Full request trace with kernel sequence and timestamps (trace store id).
- Kernel-level histograms (start_time, duration, queue_wait).
- Device perf counters sampled at 10ms granularity: SM_util, warp_occ, DRAM_bw, L2_rd/wr, tensor_core_ops.
- Scheduler telemetry: slot assignment, preemption events, admission decisions.
- Execution environment: driver version, CUDA/cuDNN/ROCm versions, kernel build flags.

Safe lab commands and snippets:
- Start a deterministic replay with kernel override:
  rwd-replay --trace-corpus traces/incident-42.tar.gz --kernel-override attention:v2 --concurrency 8 --sample-rate 1.0 --out /tmp/replay-output

- Collect perf counters with rwd-prof (example):
  rwd-prof --pid <replay-pid> --counters SM_UTIL,DRAM_BW,L2_MISS --interval_ms 10 --out profiling/case-42.json

- Example kernel-override YAML used by the replay harness:
  overrides:
    - kernel: attention
      variant: v2
      force: true

Expected artifacts (attach to incident):
1) replay-output/log.json
2) profiling/case-42.json (perf counters)
3) delta-report.csv (p50/p95/p99 deltas, occupancy deltas)
4) experimental-runbook.md (chosen remediation path)

Decision matrix (condensed):
| EvidenceScore | Action | Rollout scope | Monitoring window | Owner |
|---------------|--------|---------------|-------------------|-------|
| >= 0.7 | Emergency rollback | Canary -> Prod stop | 1 hour | Kernel-owner |
| 0.4–0.7 | Targeted A/B | 5% traffic shadow | 48 hours | Runtime-release |
| < 0.4 | Deeper instrumentation | Lab only | N/A | Profiling team |

Appendix A — Normalization constants and thresholds:
- delta_p99_normalized = min(1.0, observed_delta_p99_ms / 300)  # 300ms maps to 1.0 for scoring
- occupancy_change_normalized = min(1.0, abs(delta_occ_pct) / 40)  # 40% occupancy swing maps to 1.0
- repro_rate = fraction of lab runs that reproduce > 90th percentile effect (0..1)

Appendix B — When to escalate to security/compliance:
- If the repro experiment required production customer data to trigger: mark confidentiality=restricted and notify security for data handling clearance.
- If remediation requires hotpatching customer-facing codepaths, open Change Management with at least one reviewer from Platform Security.

Appendix C — Recommended hooks to add for future incidents (owner: runtime-observability):
- Add kernel-variant tag to trace root and ensure sampling retains tag for 48 hours post-deploy.
- Emit per-kernel occupancy delta metrics to metrics store: runtime.kernel.occupancy.delta{kernel_variant}.
- Add an automated replay job that can reconstruct the top-100 slow traces for any 24h window.
